title: The Night Market Scare
subtitle: A stabbing rumour has the market on edge; the easy answer is a curfew
coldOpen: 21:05. A fight near the night market leaves one man injured.
21:30. Forwards say three are dead and a gang is loose.
Two hundred stalls are deciding whether to open tomorrow.

briefing.grievance: Stall owners and families say the market has felt unsafe for weeks and nobody listens. Tonight’s fight turned that fear into a rumour of killings.
knownFacts: One man was injured in a fight at 21:05 and is stable in hospital.
The market employs about two thousand people, most paid daily.
Police patrols there were cut last month.
unverifiedClaims: Forwards say three people are dead and a gang is roaming.
A voice note says the police have ordered a curfew from 22:00.
briefing.responsibility: You run tonight’s response for the police and the market committee. Fear is spreading faster than facts.
briefing.objective: Make the market safe enough to open tomorrow without locking down a district on a rumour.

decisions.title: Fear is moving faster than facts
decisions.situation: The “three dead” note is in every stall owner’s phone. The committee is asking you whether to open tomorrow.

options.title: Publish the hospital count and the order log
options.preview: One injured, stable; no curfew. Sent to the committee and every market group.
options.authority: Duty of candour: say what is known and what is not
options.consequence: The committee forwards it stall to stall. Fewer shutters stay down.

options.title: Go to the market with the committee
options.preview: You walk the lanes tonight and hear the eleven unanswered complaints.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: Owners see you in their lane. The complaints finally have a listener.

options.title: Order a market curfew from 22:00
options.preview: Everything shuts; patrols enforce empty lanes.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: Two thousand daily earners lose tomorrow. The rumour looks confirmed.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Wait for the morning report
options.preview: Nothing official tonight; the voice note keeps playing.
options.consequence: By midnight half the stalls have decided not to open.

decisions.title: What really happened in lane 4?

options.title: Secure the recorder and review lane 4

options.title: Restore the night patrol tonight

options.title: Announce a gang attack and a manhunt
options.preview: A press line names a “gang” and promises sweeps across the market.
options.authority: Due process: a public charge needs verified evidence
options.consequence: Sweeps begin on the strength of a voice note.

options.title: Let the recorder loop
options.preview: Nobody copies the footage; by morning it is gone.
options.consequence: The only record of the fight overwrites itself.

o-d002-2-secure.consequence: It shows two men, not a gang. The clip is safe.

o-d002-2-patrol.title: Bring back the night patrol
o-d002-2-patrol.preview: Two foot patrols walk the lanes with volunteers.

decisions.title: Open tomorrow, or lock down?
decisions.situation: The committee will open at dawn if patrols are visible. Senior officers want the district sealed until the “gang” is caught.

options.title: Open with patrols and a lit corridor
options.preview: Lanes open at dawn with patrols, extra lights and a help desk.
options.authority: Article 19(1)(b): peaceful assembly, policed in proportion
options.consequence: The market opens. Two thousand people earn their day.

options.title: Pick up the two men from the footage
options.preview: Officers use the clip to find both men; the lanes stay open.
options.authority: Proportionality: act against the few causing harm, not the many
options.consequence: Both men are located. The market never shuts.

options.title: Seal the district until arrests
options.preview: Barricades at every lane entrance; nobody trades until the “gang” is found.
options.authority: Article 19(2)–(3): restrictions must be reasonable and specific
options.consequence: The district is sealed over a two-man fight. Stall owners start arguing with police.

rightsMoments.question: Can a whole market district be sealed because of an unverified rumour of a gang?

options.text: No. A restriction on movement and trade needs a real, specific threat, not a forwarded claim.
options.feedback: Correct. Restrictions must be proportionate to a verified risk; a rumour is not one.

options.text: Yes. Public safety always outweighs trade and movement.
options.feedback: Safety matters, but the restriction must still be necessary and proportionate to a real threat.

options.text: Yes, as long as it is lifted within a week.
options.feedback: A short duration does not make an unjustified restriction lawful.

rightsMoments.principle: Freedom of movement and the right to trade can be limited only by reasonable restrictions tied to a real threat (Article 19). Rumours do not meet that bar.
rightsMoments.why: Sealing the market would have punished two thousand earners for a two-man fight and a fake voice note.

simple.question: Can you seal the whole market because of a rumour about a gang?

options.a: No. You need a real, specific danger, not a forward.
options.b: Yes. Safety always beats trade and movement.
options.c: Yes, if it ends within a week.

feedback.a: Yes! A rumour is not a real danger.
feedback.b: Safety matters, but the danger must be real and the step fair.
feedback.c: A short ban is still unfair if the reason is false.

simple.principle: People may move and trade freely. Only a real danger can limit that.
simple.why: Sealing the market would have hurt two thousand people over a fake voice note.
